facts.statement: Leptosuchus is an extinct genus of parasuchid phytosaurs with a complex taxonomic history.
facts.quote: Leptosuchus (from Ancient Greek λεπτός (leptós), meaning "thin", and Σοῦχος (Soûkhos), meaning "Sobek") is an extinct genus of leptosuchomorph parasuchid phytosaurs with a complex taxonomical history.

facts.statement: Fossils of Leptosuchus have been found in the Dockum Group and lower Chinle Formation in Texas, New Mexico, and Arizona.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from the Dockum Group and lower Chinle Formation outcropping in Texas, New Mexico, and Arizona, United States, and date back to the Norian stage of the Late Triassic.

facts.statement: Leptosuchus lived during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from the Dockum Group and lower Chinle Formation outcropping in Texas, New Mexico, and Arizona, United States, and date back to the Norian stage of the Late Triassic.

facts.statement: The type species L. crosbiensis was named in 1922 based on material found in Texas.
facts.quote: The type species is L. crosbiensis, which was named in 1922 on the basis of material found from Texas.

facts.statement: The species L. studeri was named in 1934 based on a skull found in Potter County, Texas.
facts.quote: Another Texan species, L. studeri, was named in 1934 for a skull found in Potter County.

facts.statement: Recent studies generally classify the species L. adamanensis, L. lithodendrorum, and L. gregorii as belonging to the genus Smilosuchus.
facts.quote: More recent studies generally classify all three species as Smilosuchus.

facts.statement: Some paleontologists debate whether Leptosuchus and Machaeroprosopus are synonymous with the genus Rutiodon.
facts.quote: The close relation of Leptosuchus and Machaeroprosopus with Rutiodon has led some paleontologists to believe that the prior two were synonymous with Rutiodon, with the latter's name having seniority.

facts.statement: It is debated whether differences between Leptosuchus, Machaeroprosopus, and Rutiodon represent sexual dimorphism, growth stages, or individual variation.
facts.quote: Differing features seen in the three phytosaurs have been attributed to sexual dimorphism, differing growth stages, or individual variation, while similarities could be seen in the rostral crest and the position of the nares.

facts.statement: Leptosuchus belongs to the parent group Leptosuchomorpha.
Leptosuchus is classified within the family Parasuchidae.
Leptosuchus is classified as a reptile.
Leptosuchus lived between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)
